Exercise 2.40: (Commutation relations for the Pauli matrices) Verify the commutation relations

$$
\begin{equation*}
[X, Y]=2 i Z ; \quad[Y, Z]=2 i X ; \quad[Z, X]=2 i Y . \tag{2.73}
\end{equation*}
$$

There is an elegant way of writing this using $\epsilon_{j k l}$, the antisymmetric tensor on three indices, for which $\epsilon_{j k l}=0$ except for $\epsilon_{123}=\epsilon_{231}=\epsilon_{312}=1$, and $\epsilon_{321}=\epsilon_{213}=\epsilon_{132}=-1$:

$$
\begin{equation*}
\left[\sigma_{j}, \sigma_{k}\right]=2 i \sum_{l=1}^{3} \epsilon_{j k l} \sigma_{l} . \tag{2.74}
\end{equation*}
$$
<<<END_ITEM>>>
